item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Development of solid/quasi-solid (bio)-polymer electrolytes for sustainable rechargeable batteries - Ref.114/26/IR (Politecnico TORINO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-12 15:00
Institution: Politecnico TORINO, Torino
Field: Chemistry / 03/CHEM-06 Fondamenti chimici delle tecnologie

Within the European HIPERZAB project (GA 101115421), the research aims to develop biopolymer-based gel electrolytes for electrically rechargeable zinc-air batteries intended for stationary renewable energy storage over days or weeks. The focus will be on mildly acidic formulations and their integration into bilayer architectures with alkaline electrolytes. The objective is to correlate material composition, structure and properties to improve ionic conductivity, interfacial stability, water retention and operational lifetime. item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Engineering of Catalytic Active Sites on Nanocarbons for Enhancement of Photocatalysis (Univ. PADOVA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-16 13:00
Institution: Univ. PADOVA, Padova
Field: Chemistry / 03/CHEM-03 Chimica generale e inorganica

The research programme aims to develop catalytic systems based on non-noble metals for the selective semi-hydrogenation of acetylene to ethylene under visible light, using water as a proton source. Activities will focus on the design, synthesis and characterization of first-row transition-metal complexes and the evaluation of their activity in combination with photosensitizers. Relationships between complex structure, electrochemical properties and catalytic performance will be investigated to optimize efficiency,selectivity and stability. Spectroscopic, electrochemical and isotope-labelling studies will probe electron and proton transfer processes and the reaction mechanism. The findings…

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Synthesis and characterization of advanced materials for capture and conversion of CO2 (Univ. BRESCIA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-26 14:00
Institution: Univ. BRESCIA, Brescia
Field: Chemistry / 03/CHEM-06 Fondamenti chimici delle tecnologie

The research activity will focus on the development, synthesis, and characterization of advanced materials for CO₂ capture and conversion. The work will involve the design and preparation of innovative materials, including adsorbents, catalysts, and multifunctional materials, with tailored physicochemical properties for the selective interaction with CO₂ and its subsequent conversion into higher-value products. The materials will be characterized using spectroscopic, microscopic, telectrochemical, and surface analysis techniques, as well as evaluated through adsorption and catalytic activity tests. item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-15 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Chemistry / 03/CHEM-04 Chimica industriale

The ultimate objective of the REACT-FIBER project is to develop, validate and demonstrate at pilot scale an integrated, industrially scalable technological supply chain for the high-value recycling of Carbon Fiber Sheet Molding Compound (CF-SMC) materials. The activities planned under this assignment relate to OR2: Analysis of the quality of carbon fibers recycled from SMC, with particular reference to: • A2.1 – Optimization of carbon fiber recycling from cured SMC • A2.2 – Assessment of the feasibility of extending the recycling process to uncured scrap

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Development of Biomimetic and Edible Nanozyme for the Ultrasensitive and Selective Determination of Glucose (Univ. BARI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-10 23:55
Institution: Univ. BARI, Roma
Field: Chemistry / 03/CHEM-01 Chimica analitica, ambientale e dei beni culturali

The research activity will focus on the development and characterization of biomimetic and edible nanozymes with catalytic activity toward glucose oxidation, to be integrated into electrochemical platforms for its ultrasensitive and selective determination. In particular, nanomaterials with enzyme-like activity will be developed, also through the use of biocompatible and naturally derived components, and their integration into edible conductive formulations will be investigated. item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-23 12:00
Institution: Univ. PAVIA, Pavia
Field: Chemistry / 03/CHEM-05 Chimica organica

The research program involves: 1) the study of photoinduced processes for the valorization of bioplastics under metal-free conditions; 2) the development of photoorganocatalyzed processes for the modification of the backbone of bioplastic materials; 3) the implementation of processes for the controlled depolymerization of bioplastic materials mediated by bio-based catalysts.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Novel Photocatalytic Strategies for Organoboron Chemistry - 2026_IDR_DCMC_22 (Politecnico MILANO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-16 12:00
Institution: Politecnico MILANO, Milan
Field: Chemistry / 03/CHEM-06 Fondamenti chimici delle tecnologie

The project aims to develop innovative photocatalytic strategies for the sustainable synthesis of organoboron compounds (OBCs), fundamental in organic chemistry and crucial for the pharmaceutical and materials sectors. Since traditional methods based on carbanion chemistry are poorly sustainable, an efficient and eco-compatible approach driven by visible light is proposed. Photocatalysis grants access to open-shell intermediates under mild conditions, a reactivity suited to boron substrates, whose vacant p orbital favours radical stabilisation. item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-09 23:59
Institution: Univ. BASILICATA, Potenza
Field: Chemistry / 03/CHEM-07 Chimica farmaceutica, tossicologica, nutraceutico-alimentare, delle fermentazioni e dei prodotti per il benessere e per la salute

The project will focus on the study of the effects induced by exposure to environmental contaminants in complex biological systems, with the aim of understanding the cellular and molecular mechanisms associated with the risk of chronic diseases. The activities will include sample preparation and treatment, the analysis of biological responses under different experimental conditions, and the evaluation of biochemical and metabolic alterations induced by exposure.
